blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: time complexity — How an algorithm's work grows with input size.
O(n) — Work proportional to input count.
O(log n) — Work proportional to the number of halvings.
O(n²) — Quadratic growth, often nested loops.
trade-off — A benefit balanced against another cost.

blocks.title: Count what grows
blocks.text: Big O describes how work increases with input size, not the exact milliseconds on one computer.

blocks.title: Compare search
blocks.text: Linear search can take n checks; binary search on sorted input roughly halves the remaining candidates each step.

blocks.title: Compare sorting
blocks.text: A simple nested comparison loop can be O(n²), whereas merge sort is O(n log n).

blocks.title: Model solution
